Read this before you start

  1. The paper has 50 questions. Use the timing that matches your test arrangements.
  2. Read every passage and question carefully before choosing an answer.
  3. Choose one answer for each question.
  4. You may move backwards and forwards, change answers and flag questions before you finish.
  5. Each question is worth 1 mark. There is no negative marking.
  6. Answers and explanations are shown only after you finish the paper.
  7. This is general skills practice, not an official, provider-specific, age-standardised or pass-prediction test.

Balanced mode is best for comparing raw scores. Adaptive mode uses sufficient attempted-answer evidence to adjust later practice; it does not claim to diagnose ability.
